model.vision: A simple, dependable todo list that a small team's people and agent tooling can rely on.

objectives.statement: People never lose work they have recorded: every todo is intact, in wording and completion, whenever they return to the list, with zero todos lost to closing, reloading or restarting.
Keeping the list true costs people almost nothing: a first-time user can take a todo from entry through correction and completion to removal without training or assistance.
People always know where they stand: at any moment, what remains to be done is visible at a glance and is never misstated, however they choose to review the list.
Finished work stops competing for attention: people can retire it in bulk whenever they choose, with no unfinished todo ever lost in doing so.
The team's other tooling, agents included, can work the list on people's behalf, completing every list task a person can, with the same outcome.
The team can start on the first day of release, working the list as an ordinary destination of its own or embedded among the tools it already uses.

model.mission: Settle one meaning for each thing that can be done to a todo, and keep every todo in one lasting record that outlives any session. Let people and agent tooling alike work that same record under those same rules, so that another way of reaching or reviewing the list never changes what the list means.

deliverySurfaces.source: an MCP Apps surface so it can be embedded the same way our other MCP-hosted UIs are
reachable both as an ordinary web API
as an MCP surface, so our other agent tooling can drive it too

items.definition: Someone on the team who keeps a todo list, whether working it directly or through agent tooling.
The small group of people who use the product, each keeping their own todo list.
The team's other tooling, agents included, that works a person's todo list on that person's behalf, under the same rules and with the same outcome.
A tool the team already uses, inside which a person can work the todo list without leaving it.
One thing a person means to get done, known by its wording and its completion.
All of one person's todos, in the order they were recorded; never shared with another person.
The free text that says what a todo is; it is never blank.
Offered text that is empty or holds only whitespace, and so cannot be a todo's wording.
Whether a todo is done (completed) or still to be done (active).
A todo that is still to be done.
A todo that has been marked done and is still on the todo list.
A way of looking at the todo list: All (every todo), Active (only active todos) or Completed (only completed todos). Exactly one is current, and the person can always tell which.
How many active todos the whole todo list holds right now, whichever view is current.
Put a new active todo at the end of the todo list; blank wording records nothing.
Replace an existing todo's wording without changing its completion or its place in the todo list; settling on blank wording removes the todo.
Give up a rewording in progress, so the todo keeps its original wording.
Take one todo off the todo list for good, whatever its completion, leaving every other todo untouched.
Mark one active todo as done, leaving every other todo untouched.
Turn one completed todo back into an active todo, leaving every other todo untouched.
In one act, complete every todo; or, when every todo is already completed, reopen every todo.
In one act, remove every completed todo from the todo list, leaving every active todo untouched; with no completed todos, nothing changes.
Look at the todo list under a chosen view; choosing a view changes only which todos are shown, never the todos themselves.
Come back to the todo list after closing, reloading or restarting, and find every todo with the same wording and completion.
The activity of deciding whether offered wording is blank and what follows: nothing is recorded when the todo is new, and the todo is removed when it is being reworded.
The activity of deciding, from the completion of every todo, whether marking the whole list completes all of them or reopens all of them.
The activity of determining which todos a sweep removes: those completed at that moment, and no others.
The activity of determining which todos belong in a view, from each todo's completion.
The activity of working out the remaining count from the whole todo list, anew whenever an act changes which todos are active.
Place a newly recorded todo in the lasting record, at the end of its todo list.
Put a todo's new wording into the lasting record in place of the old.
Set the completion of one or many todos in the lasting record, as a single act.
Take one or many todos out of the lasting record for good, as a single act.
Obtain a person's todo list from the lasting record, with every todo's wording, completion and place.
The one enduring home of every todo list, outliving any visit, closure, reload or restart, and the same record for people and agent tooling alike.

items.name: List-work volatility
items.rationale: What: the sequence of acts by which a person or agent tooling keeps a todo list true (record, reword, complete, reopen, mark whole list, sweep, return). Why: it is the part a team asks to change first once it uses the product daily; the brief itself leaves the shape of the product open. Likelihood: high, several times a year in early use. Effect: unencapsulated, each new or reordered act is rebuilt separately on all four delivery surfaces and their outcomes drift apart, breaking objective 5. Grounding: mission objectives 2, 4, 5; behavior reference sections 1-6. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors (scrubbedRequirements) exist on this branch to trace to; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

items.name: List-rule volatility
items.rationale: What: the judgements that decide what an act means: what blank wording leads to, whether marking the whole list completes or reopens, which todos a sweep retires and what becomes of them. Why: todo products differ here (a blank rewording may be refused, restored or treated as removal; finished work may be kept or discarded), and the team is likely to revisit these choices as it lives with them. Likelihood: moderate, an adjustment every year or so. Effect: unencapsulated, a rule is restated in every act and surface, so people and agents get different outcomes for the same act, against the mission's 'one meaning' and objectives 4 and 5. Grounding: mission; behavior reference sections 1, 2, 5, 6. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors exist on this branch; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

items.name: List-record volatility
items.rationale: What: where and how the lasting record is kept, and what it holds for a todo. Why: the brief fixes only that todos survive and leaves the todo's shape open; the reference says a todo has 'at minimum' wording and completion. Likelihood: moderate, a change to what is held within a year or two and a change of storage technology once or twice in the system's life. Effect: unencapsulated, storage detail leaks into every act and any move puts recorded todos at risk, breaking objective 1. Grounding: mission objective 1; behavior reference section 9. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors exist on this branch; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

items.name: Access-channel volatility
items.rationale: What: the way a person or agent tooling reaches the list. Why: at release the same list is already reached four different ways (an ordinary web app, embedded in a host tool, a web API, an MCP surface) by different users at once, and the set is open-ended as the team's tools vary. Likelihood: high; the four coexist on day one, and host tools and agent conventions are still young. Effect: unencapsulated, a channel's conventions leak into the list's rules, so adding or altering one touches all the others and outcomes stop matching, breaking objectives 5 and 6. Grounding: mission objectives 5, 6 and its delivery surfaces; founder brief, delivery paragraph. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors exist on this branch; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

items.name: Review-perspective volatility
items.rationale: What: how a person chooses to look over the list and gauge where they stand. Why: people review differently at the same moment ('however they like to review their list'), agent tooling wants an answer rather than a screen, and the mission expects further ways of reviewing. Likelihood: moderate, a new perspective or summary every year or so. Effect: unencapsulated, each surface selects and counts for itself, so the remaining count or the contents of a view disagree between surfaces, breaking objective 3. This is the weakest entry: today's three views alone are merely variable (see rejected), and it stands on the mission's 'another way of reviewing' only. Grounding: mission objective 3; behavior reference sections 7, 8. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors exist on this branch; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

items.name: List-authority volatility
items.rationale: What: who may see or change which todo list, keyed on the caller the platform supplies. Why: callers already differ at one time: a person works their own list, while agent tooling works it on that person's behalf; and the sources disagree on reach (the brief says 'our team', the reference says a single user/session; mission review left this for founder confirmation). Likelihood: moderate to high, since the open question must be answered and any answer may be revised as more tooling is trusted. Effect: unencapsulated, ownership checks scatter over every act and channel, and one missed check exposes or alters another person's list. Grounding: mission objective 5; glossary Todo list and Agent tooling; founder brief. This covers business authority only, never sign-in. Traces are empty because no Required Behaviors exist on this branch; not claimed as longevity-grounded. Add B-NN traces once they exist.

rejected.name: Current three views (All, Active, Completed)
rejected.reason: Three fixed selections decided by one completion value; a condition handles them. Only the open-ended way of reviewing is kept.

rejected.name: Active or completed state of a todo
rejected.reason: A single two-valued fact on a todo; data, with no structural consequence.

rejected.name: Wording length and whitespace trimming
rejected.reason: A bound or trim on free text is a value check inside the wording judgement.

rejected.name: Rewording gestures (double-click, Enter, Escape, loss of focus)
rejected.reason: Interaction detail local to one surface; the reference itself allows 'or otherwise explicitly activates'.

rejected.name: Number of todos and people
rejected.reason: The brief is for a small team; the expected range is a capacity setting and does not alter the structure.

rejected.name: Todos are recorded, completed and removed at all
rejected.reason: Every todo product does this; without it the product is not a todo list.

rejected.name: Todos outlive the visit
rejected.reason: Any usable todo product keeps its list; losing it is never a wanted variation. How it is kept is List-record.

rejected.name: Due dates, priorities, tags and categories
rejected.reason: The reference puts them out of scope and says they must not be assumed.

rejected.name: Sharing a list among people
rejected.reason: Multi-user sharing is explicitly out of scope; only who may act on one person's list is evidenced.

rejected.name: Reordering todos by hand
rejected.reason: Drag-to-reorder is explicitly out of scope; order is simply that of recording.

rejected.name: Undo and redo history
rejected.reason: Explicitly out of scope; nothing in the brief asks for restoring past acts beyond reopening.

rejected.name: Offline work and later reconciliation
rejected.reason: Offline sync is explicitly out of scope and the record lives behind a real service.

rejected.name: How people and agents are authenticated
rejected.reason: The platform's Security utility and front door already own who is acting; encapsulating it again would duplicate a utility.

rejected.name: Hosting and deployment arrangement
rejected.reason: The brief asks for it to be built the usual way; the platform treats the deployment scenario as configuration, so no system change is evidenced.

rejected.name: Notifying people of unfinished todos
rejected.reason: No source asks for reminders; the count is shown on the list and nothing is sent.

rejected.name: Reporting on completed work
rejected.reason: A reflex reporting block; the founder wants finished work swept away, not analysed.

rejected.name: Live refresh across several open surfaces
rejected.reason: The count must follow acts on the list, but no source asks an idle surface to follow acts made elsewhere.

rejected.name: Host tool embedding conventions
rejected.reason: Folded into Access-channel volatility: a host tool is one way of reaching the list.

rejected.name: Agent tooling conventions
rejected.reason: Folded into Access-channel volatility: a change in how agents call is a channel change, the acts being identical.

rejected.name: Todo composition
rejected.reason: Folded into List-record volatility: what is held for a todo changes with the record that holds it.

rejected.name: Simultaneous work by a person and agent tooling
rejected.reason: Folded into List-record volatility: the glossary settles completion and retirement as single acts on the one record.

rejected.name: Whole-list marking behavior
rejected.reason: Folded into List-rule volatility: choosing to complete or reopen is one of its judgements.

rejected.name: Disposition of finished todos
rejected.reason: Folded into List-rule volatility: what a sweep selects and does with its selection is a rule of meaning.

rejected.name: Remaining-count calculation
rejected.reason: Folded into Review-perspective volatility: the count is one summary of where a person stands.

decisions.essenceRationale: This is what the product is for: whatever is asked of the list, by a person or by agent tooling, is given one settled meaning and one lasting effect. Every person on the team relies on it; it stays the same when acts, rules, storage or ways of reaching the list change; and it is what sets a dependable shared-rule list apart from a toy that lives in one browser. It abstracts every act the sources name, single or whole-list (record, reword, remove, complete, reopen, mark all, sweep), none of which is the essence alone. It crosses List-work, List-rule, List-record, List-authority and Access-channel volatility, the last because the one flow serves both declared actors.

decisions.essenceRationale: A list is kept only so that someone can trust what it says: people record work in order to stop carrying it in their heads, and that bargain holds only if what remains is never misstated. Every person needs it on every visit; it outlives any particular view, summary or surface; and one answer drawn from one lasting record, whoever asks and however, is what a list held in each browser cannot give. It abstracts choosing a view, reading the count and returning after an absence, and is distinct from keeping the list true because it never changes a todo. It crosses Review-perspective, List-record, List-authority and Access-channel volatility.

4.critiqueNotes:
The two cores (Keep the List True, Take Stock) are right. Both are real abstractions with real essence arguments, so keep them as they are. The fixes below concern what the actor is shown, plus one channel-shaped entry.

REQUIRED

1. Channel-shaped use case: `work-the-list-embedded-in-a-host-tool`. Its own rejection reason says "only the channel differs", and its flow is keep-the-list-true with "inside the host tool" added. Remove it as a use case. The founder's MCP Apps ask is not lost: it is mission objective 6 and the `mcpApp` delivery surface, and the architecture must serve both cores there. The entry also omitted reviewing the list while embedded, which is what happens when a channel is drawn as a use case.

2. Agent tooling asks, but the outcome goes to someone else. Both cores declare actor `agent-tooling`, and their first act reads "Person, directly or through agent tooling, asks...". Every act and outcome is nonetheless linked to `person` only (`see-list`, `told-refused`, `see-standing`). As drawn, an agent-made request enters through no act of the agent's and ends in nothing the agent is told. Objective 5 promises the tooling the same outcome. The essence claim that Access-channel volatility is crossed "because the one flow serves both declared actors" rests on this too.
   - In `keep-the-list-true` and `take-stock`: give Agent tooling its own linked act (for example, a second start-rooted entry) and its own linked outcome and refusal `sendSignal`s. Drop "directly or through agent tooling" from the Person's act.
   - In the eight human-worded variations (`add-a-todo`, `reword-a-todo`, `delete-a-todo`, `mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done`, `mark-everything-done-at-once`, `clear-completed-todos`, `switch-views`, `see-how-many-todos-are-left`) and in `come-back-and-find-the-list-intact`: drop the declared `agent-tooling` actor, or link its acts and outcomes. Do not declare an actor the diagram never uses.
   - `let-agent-tooling-drive-the-list` may stay. It has its own actor and the on-behalf-of authority question, so I do not read it as channel-shaped. Restate its rejection reason on that basis rather than "another caller and channel".

3. Outcomes that are not the ones the raw use case promises. Different branches merge into one generic label, so a test derived from them cannot tell right behavior from wrong. Give each differing branch its own outcome `sendSignal`/`objectNode`, or put the branch's result on an `objectNode` with `inState`:
   - `mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done-P1` (todo already gone): "Person sees the todo's completion as it now stands" is impossible, because there is no such todo. Say the list is shown without it. P2 should say the todo is shown completed or reopened as asked, with every other todo unchanged.
   - `add-a-todo-P1` / `P2`: one conditional label ("cleared if a todo was recorded") covers both. P1: the new todo is shown active, last on the list, count up by one, entry field cleared. P2 (blank): the list and count are shown unchanged.
   - `reword-a-todo-P2` / `P3` / `P4`: all read "the list as it now stands". P2: the todo shows its new wording, same completion and place. P4 (blank): the todo is no longer on the list. P3: nothing differs.
   - `mark-everything-done-at-once-P1` / `P3` / `P2`: P1: every todo is shown completed, none remaining. P3: every todo is shown active, all remaining. P2: the list is still empty.
   - `clear-completed-todos-P2` / `P1`: P2: no completed todo remains, every active todo is still there, count unchanged. P1: the list is unchanged.
   - `let-agent-tooling-drive-the-list-P1` / `P2` / `P3`: "the same outcome a person would see" names no outcome. State it for a changing act, for an act with nothing to do, and for a review (the todos in the view asked for, plus the count).
   - `keep-the-list-true`: distinguish at least "the act's effect is shown" from "nothing changed" (P3).

NON-BLOCKING (no need to answer to pass)

a. `add-a-todo` shows "the list as it now stands" but no node recalls the list, unlike its siblings.
b. Reference section 7: an act does not change the current view. After an act, "the list" means the todos in the view the person was in (completing under Active makes the todo leave that view). Worth a note on `keep-the-list-true`.
c. Reference section 2: opening a rewording shows the current wording. Carry this to the architecture.
d. `come-back-and-find-the-list-intact` does not show which view is current, though reference section 7 says it is always visible.
e. Carry to the architecture: every select/judge action (`select-view`, `select-sweep`, `judge-*`) needs a real call of its own beside `recall-list`.
f. No Required Behaviors exist on this branch, so I checked the raw list against the founder brief and behavior reference, and the staged mission, glossary and volatilities. It is complete against the brief's nine asks. The founder still needs to confirm list authority scope (team vs single user).
